title: Mini-Project: Dispatch Loop for Skeptic Reviews
objective: Apply GSD-2 architecture concepts (state machine, dispatch pipeline, context engineering, auto mode) to extend the skeptic workflow with a dispatch loop that reads state, routes focused reviews, and tracks coverage until complete

content.value:
Look at the skeptic command you have built across five modules. In Module 1 you wrote the command spec. In Module 2 you added the handler. In Module 3 you made findings persist. In Module 4 you added orchestration with parallel review subagents and aggregation. In Module 5 you added quality verification that checks the review's own output.

But every time you run skeptic, it executes the same steps in the same order. It does not look at what it already reviewed. It does not decide what to focus on next based on project state. It does not scope its context to the area under review. Compare that to GSD-2's auto mode from Lesson 4: auto mode reads state from disk, decides what task to dispatch, gives that task only the context it needs, marks it complete, and loops until the milestone is done.

Module 6 closes this gap. You will add a dispatch loop to your skeptic workflow -- a mechanism that reads review state, decides what area to review next, dispatches a focused review with scoped context, tracks coverage, and repeats until all areas are reviewed. This is the auto mode pattern applied to code review.

content.value:
Below is a workflow template that adds a dispatch loop to your existing skeptic workflow. Press C to copy, then integrate it into your workflow at ~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/skeptic.md. The key addition is a dispatch loop mechanism that replaces static review steps with a dynamic cycle: read state, pick next area, dispatch focused review, update tracking, repeat.

Place this mechanism so it controls how reviews are dispatched -- it can replace or wrap your existing wave-based review steps from Module 4. The specific review areas, context scoping strategy, and loop structure are yours to customize.

<!-- Dispatch loop for skeptic reviews (inspired by GSD-2 auto mode) -->

<step name="dispatch_loop">
**Dispatch focused reviews in a loop until coverage is complete.**

## State Tracking
Maintain a coverage map of review areas and their status:
- architecture: pending
- conventions: pending
- dependencies: pending
- error-handling: pending
(Add or remove areas based on the project under review)

## Dispatch Logic
For each iteration of the loop:
1. Read the coverage map to find the next pending area
2. Route to a focused review for that specific area
3. Provide scoped context -- only files and patterns relevant to this area

## Context Scoping
Each dispatched review receives narrowed context:
- Filter files to only those relevant to the review area
- Inject area-specific review criteria
- Do NOT pass the entire project -- scope to what matters

## Coverage Tracking
After each dispatched review completes:
- Mark the area as reviewed in the coverage map
- Record findings from this review pass
- Check if unreviewed areas remain

## Loop Continuation
Repeat the dispatch cycle:
- If pending areas remain -> dispatch next review
- If all areas are reviewed -> exit loop, proceed to aggregation
- Termination: all areas marked complete or coverage threshold met
</step>
content.focus: Dispatch loop step with state tracking, dispatch logic, context scoping, coverage tracking, and termination

content.value:
Make it yours. The six structural requirements that verification checks for are:

1. State tracking -- reads or tracks project state to decide what to review next
2. Dispatch logic -- routes work to focused review subagents
3. Context scoping -- injects scoped context into each dispatched review (not full project)
4. Coverage tracking -- tracks what has been reviewed to avoid duplication
5. Loop iteration -- loops or iterates until review coverage is complete
6. Termination condition -- has a condition that ends the dispatch loop

Everything else -- the specific review areas, how context is scoped, the loop mechanism, whether you use a counter or a map or a checklist, how many iterations, what triggers termination -- is your creative decision. Verification checks structure, not content.
